basis: Inherited abnormalities of coagulation; vascular thrombosis and bleeding-related organ injuries are subtype-dependent.
Structural or functional lymphatic vessel defects define primary lymphedema; swelling alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Focal epilepsy arising from an acquired structural brain abnormality.
Mechanical restriction of ocular movement causes strabismus.
Ectopic implantation in the uterine horn is an obstetric and reproductive condition; hemorrhagic complications do not define another axis.
Congenital muscle dysfunction and extensive contractures define the syndrome; intellectual disability and developmental impairment are major features.
Intrinsic platelet hyperresponsiveness causes thrombocytopenia and bleeding; mucocutaneous bleeding does not establish skin or gastrointestinal disease.
Prostatic abscess and infection-associated malakoplakia support the infection axis; the prostate and seminal vesicles have no anatomical axis.
Hereditary bradykinin-mediated angioedema affects skin and subcutis; it is not immune-mediated. Episodic lip swelling does not establish GI damage.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with speech delay and neurological findings; the causal gene alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Isolated lens displacement defines the disease; skeletal and cardiovascular abnormalities are below 30% in the supplied phenotypes.
Defining malformations involve external ears, finger bones, toenails and dermatoglyphics; these establish the three primary axes.
A depressive disorder is purely psychiatric for this scheme; biological attribution and neurological ancestry do not establish organ damage.
Isolated congenital hearing impairment from auditory system abnormalities; language acquisition difficulties follow deafness.
Microcephaly, developmental impairment, seizures and ataxia define CNS disease; weakness and pes planus (2/4) do not establish direct muscle or bone injury.
Brain malformations and developmental impairment define the neurological component; postaxial polydactyly is a defining skeletal malformation.
CNS toxicity and cardiac conduction or contractile toxicity are the principal manifestations of systemic local anesthetic poisoning; other targets are agent-specific.
Predominantly immune-mediated inflammation of the intermediate uvea; associated systemic disorders are separate diseases or uncommon.
A vascular endothelial neoplasm characteristically arising in dermis and subcutis; distant organ involvement is rare.
Congenital developmental malformation of pulmonary airways and lung tissue.
CNS hypomyelination and neurodegeneration define the disease; skeletal muscle atrophy is documented in 4/4 patients. Feeding symptoms alone do not establish GI injury.
Benign tumour of the tonsil, a pharyngeal site within the pulmonary axis; lymphoid location alone does not imply immune or blood disease.
Chronic immune-mediated airway inflammation and variable airflow obstruction define asthma.
Malignant smooth muscle tumour arising in the oesophagus; smooth muscle histology does not establish skeletal muscle disease or infection.
Complete absence of gonadal tissue entails loss of gonadal endocrine function, supporting the endocrine axis beyond reproductive anatomy.
